A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same multi-scale bilateral-grid Gaussian-splatting work, with readable text, equations, figures and tables. v3.pdf ends after its references despite referring to appendix details; v4.pdf supplies Appendices A-C. The supplied material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original reconstruction, novel-view synthesis, geometry, efficiency and ablation results across Waymo, NuScenes, Argoverse and PandaSet in Tables 1-5 and Figures 3-6.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmark experiments and adds challenging-scene evaluations, per-scene results and vehicle-specific measurements in Table 3 and Appendices B-C.

M1.justification: The three-level grid architecture, luminance guidance, slicing, transformation composition and Gaussian scene representation are retained. Regularization and temporal interpolation already appear in v3's method description. Appendix A supplies previously missing specifications of these components without establishing a change to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: The four datasets and reconstruction/NVS tasks remain. v4 adds targeted extreme-condition coverage through challenging Argoverse, Waymo and PandaSet scenarios, including rain, glare and severe lighting transitions (Table 3; Appendix C.3). The newly listed sequences for the original benchmarks are documentation, not evidence that their coverage changed.

E2.justification: The main comparator set is retained: v3's Baseline corresponds to OmniRe, alongside appearance codes, bilateral grids, ChatSim and StreetGS. However, the human/vehicle comparisons in v3 Tables 1 and 3 lose their baseline, AC and BG entries; v4 Tables 10-13 retain only the proposed method's class-specific scores. The new aggregate vehicle comparison does not restore those original comparisons.

E3.justification: v4 extends the four-dataset comparison to LPIPS and NVS SSIM, introduces challenging-scene subgroups and a 20-scene masked vehicle-geometry evaluation, and revises the tested grid configurations. Section 4.2 also changes the reported Depth metric from L2 error to median squared depth error. This establishes a reporting/protocol revision, not that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Tables 3 and 16-19 add targeted robustness evaluations under extreme photometric conditions and vehicle-specific geometry analysis. Table 5 replaces the enlarged three-level grid ablation with a single (8,8,4) grid to examine the importance of the hierarchy. Figures 7-8 add photometric error-map comparisons. These substantially extend the retained guidance-resolution and regularization analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard errors or significance tests. The additional per-scene results in v4 provide individual outcomes rather than a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Matched headline full-image and geometry values, along with Table 2, remain unchanged. v4 adds extensive per-scene scores, metric entries, challenging-scene and vehicle results, while replacing an ablation and removing class-specific baseline entries. For example, new Table 3 reports challenging-scene reconstruction PSNR of 26.84/28.13 and CD of 0.650/0.523 for OmniRe/Ours. Some appendix averages conflict with retained main-table values, including Waymo Depth: 0.467 in Table 7 versus 0.477 in Table 1.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds explicit mathematical specifications for the total regularized objective, grid-size-dependent TV weighting, inverse-transformation circle loss and temporal interpolation (Equations 10-16). v3 names these components but lacks the referenced appendix formulations. This extends the formal specification without adding a theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contribution: a hierarchical bilateral grid unifying appearance codes and bilateral grids, improving driving-scene geometry through better photometric consistency across the same four datasets. The expanded conclusion and stronger wording do not materially redefine this contribution.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations about stronger benefits under extreme photometric conditions and on reflective vehicles. It attributes full-resolution guidance degradation to possible noise overfitting and single-grid weakness to missing coarse-level stabilization. The limitations now connect fast/non-rigid-object difficulties to LiDAR-camera misalignment. Conversely, the explicit qualification about worse Argoverse human SSIM is removed.

D1.justification: Appendices A-B supply substantial information absent from v3: sensor counts, sequence identifiers, camera-specific crops, regularization specifications, example per-level learning rates and coarse/medium-grid interpolation details. Table 1 also specifies the standalone BG size. These are largely disclosures of existing implementation choices. The learning-rate examples nevertheless contradict the accompanying coarse-versus-fine ordering; hardware and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds eight references, including UniCalib, PUGS, Simulate Any Radar, ORV and SceneCraft, mainly to contextual citation lists. The existing references and the positioning around balancing global appearance correction with local adaptability are retained.

P1.justification: Sections 4.2-4.4 substantially rewrite the experimental narrative, reorganize the quantitative discussion and condense the histogram explanation. The conclusion is expanded, captions are extensively edited, affiliations are updated and Appendices A-C introduce a new document hierarchy. This is substantial editorial restructuring beyond the added experimental content.

P2.justification: Table 1 combines retained reconstruction and full-image NVS results in a redesigned display; Table 3 becomes the challenging-scene table. v4 adds Tables 6-19 and Figures 7-11, revises captions and table emphasis, and relocates displays. Appendix floats interrupt Section A.1 across several pages, and Tables 14-15 mislabel the NVS and geometry column groups.

improvement.justification: v4 supplies implementation and dataset details missing from v3's referenced appendices and adds useful targeted robustness and vehicle-geometry evidence. These improve reproducibility and support for the central claim. However, removed class-specific baseline comparisons, mislabeled columns in Tables 14-15, contradictory learning-rate ordering in Appendix A.1.4 and inconsistent main/appendix averages limit the gains. The evidence supports a net improvement, but not an unqualified substantial one.
